judul: Multimodal Radar-Vision for Oil Palm Fresh Fruit Bunch Ripeness Classification
abstrak: This work presents a multimodal radar-vision framework for non-destructive ripeness classification of oil palm fresh fruit bunches (FFBs) under field conditions. A continuous wave 2.4 GHz radar and a digital scale capture backscattered power and bunch mass as internal cues related to dielectric properties and growth, while RGB images provide external color and texture information. Radar-weight features (power, weight, and power-to-weight ratio) are modeled using an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) classifier, and a YOLOv8-Nano detector is trained using an expert-annotated RGB dataset to localize and classify bunches into four maturity stages (Unripe, Underripe, Ripe, Overripe). Decision-level late fusion combines the class-probability outputs of both branches through mean, weighted, and stacking schemes. Experiments on radar-weight data (255 samples per class) acquired at a commercial loading ramp show that the unimodal radar-weight and vision models reach 89.9% and 94.3% accuracy, respectively, with YOLOv8-Nano achieving mAP@0.5 of 0.99. The best fusion configuration, based on stacking, attains 96.9% accuracy and 97.3% F1-macro, demonstrating that radar-weight information provides complementary evidence that stabilizes vision-based grading and supports more consistent harvest decisions.

judul: Deep Learning-Based Coconut Ripeness Classification and Yield Estimation using YOLO and Kalman Filtering
sumber: 2025 International Conference on Sensors and Related Networks Sennet 2025 Special Focus on Digital Healthcare 64220
abstrak: Accurate detection and classification of coconuts according to their ripeness stages are essential for optimizing agricultural harvesting practices, reducing manual labor, and increasing economic efficiency. The ripeness of coconuts significantly influences their commercial value, nutritional content, and suitability for various products such as coconut water, coconut milk, and oil extraction. However, manual inspection for ripeness determination is labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to inaccuracies. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a deep learning-based methodology employing YOLOv11 integrated with the Kalman Filter-Hungarian Algorithm, YOLOv8, and a custom-designed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to accurately identify coconuts at three distinct ripeness stages: immature, mid-ripe, and fully ripe. An open-source coconut dataset was utilized and enhanced through data augmentation techniques, including rotation, scaling, and color adjustments, to improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of the models across varying environmental and lighting conditions. The models were trained and rigorously evaluated using standard object detection metrics, specifically mean Average Precision (mAP50 and mAP50:95). Furthermore, the proposed approach was extended to facilitate automated counting of coconuts using different tracking methodologies, demonstrating practical applicability and potential integration into real-time agricultural monitoring systems. Experimental results illustrate that the proposed deep learning models effectively differentiate coconut ripeness stages, providing a significant advancement for precision agriculture and automation in coconut farming.

judul: DETECTION AND SEQUENCE OF COLLECTING LOOSE OIL PALM FRUIT USING DEEP LEARNING TECHNIQUE
abstrak: This paper uses YOLOv7 to detect and collect loose palm fruits with an autonomous harvesting robot. YOLOv7 was chosen due to its high accuracy and real-time detection capability. Data from high-resolution cameras in oil palm plantations are annotated to create a robust training set. Key hyperparameters such as Anchor, Learning Rate, and Weight Decay are fine-tuned to see which performs well in object detection. The robot uses YOLOv7 to detect fruits, prioritizing picking based on the coordinates of the bounding box. Hyperparameter set A excels in detection accuracy and precision, while set B is slightly better in bounding box prediction. MAP50 is 0.866 and 0.823 for sets A and B, respectively. The optimized model significantly improves the efficiency of the robot in real-time harvesting.

judul: Blueberry Maturity Detection in Natural Orchard Environments Using an Improved YOLOv11n Network
abstrak: To meet the growing demand for automated blueberry harvesting in smart agriculture, this study proposes an improved lightweight detection network, termed M-YOLOv11n, for fast and accurate blueberry maturity detection in complex natural environments. The proposed model enhances feature representation through an improved lightweight multi-scale design, enabling more effective extraction of fruit features under complex orchard conditions. In addition, attention-based feature refinement is incorporated to emphasize discriminative ripeness-related cues while suppressing background interference. These design choices improve robustness to scale variation and occlusion, addressing the limitations of conventional lightweight detectors in detecting small and partially occluded fruits. By incorporating MsBlock and the attention mechanism, M-YOLOv11n achieves improved detection accuracy without significantly increasing computational cost. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model attains 97.0% mAP50 on the validation set and maintains robust performance under challenging conditions such as occlusion and varying illumination, achieving 96.5% mAP50. With an inference speed of 176.6 FPS, the model satisfies both accuracy and real-time requirements for blueberry maturity detection. Compared with YOLOv11n, M-YOLOv11n increases the parameter count only marginally from 2.60 M to 2.61 M, while maintaining high inference efficiency. These results indicate that the proposed method is suitable for real-time deployment on embedded vision systems in smart agricultural harvesting robots and supports early yield estimation in complex field environments.

judul: Integrating Advanced Attention Mechanisms into YOLO11 for Accurate Blueberry Fruit Detection
sumber: 33rd IEEE Conference on Signal Processing and Communications Applications Siu 2025 Proceedings
abstrak: The accurate detection of blueberries across varying ripeness stages is pivotal for orchard management, yield estimation, and automated harvesting. However, natural orchard conditions featuring complex backgrounds, variable illumination, and extensive occlusion remain challenging for object detection algorithms. This study presents an enhanced version of YOLO11 that incorporates two advanced attention mechanisms, Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) and ResBlock + Convolutional Block Attention Mechanism (CBAM), to improve the detection accuracy for three classes of blueberry maturity (fully ripe, half-ripe, and unripe). We trained and validated a dataset of 8000 images (6000 for training and 2000 for testing) captured under normal daylight orchard environments, yielding 141312 bounding boxes (17.7 per image) annotated blueberry instances. The experimental results demonstrate that both attention modules significantly boost precision and recall, particularly in partial occlusion and variable lighting scenarios. The ResBlock+CBAM variant achieved a slight edge in the mean average precision (mAP) at a modest computational overhead, whereas the ECA-based network retained faster inference. Thorough studies confirmed the benefits of advanced augmentation (mosaic, mixup) and each attention module on orchard-based feature extraction. Our proposed architectures provide practical solutions for large-scale orchard deployment, contributing to efficient automated fruit management and harvesting.

judul: Efficient Iterative Semi-supervised Object Detection Training for Counting of Fruits and Vegetables
abstrak: Object recognition could be successfully applied to problems such as object counting [3]. This transition makes this kind of technology interesting for numerous industries where automation and quality assurance based on visual information are possible. A major limitation to the practical usage of object recognition models is that each time the data is changed e.g. new classes are added, the model must be retrained which usually requires manual annotation of the new data. This entails not only a continuous annotation effort, which leads to higher costs but also an increased deployment period for updated models. In this paper, we address the issue of reducing the manual effort for annotation based on the example of fruits and vegetables recognition and counting in retail applications. Furthermore, we present an iterative semi-supervised training strategy for handling this task. We achieve a reduction of the manual effort of more than 60% while maintaining the counting accuracy of 83% on 36 different object classes.
